answer: A PoA registry can require every agent identity to present a fresh, hardware-rooted attestation whose MRENCLAVE matches approved enclave code, then bind enrollment to the attested platform key. This raises Sybil costs: duplicating a VM or copying software cannot forge that key; under one-identity-per-platform rules, an attacker must obtain additional attested silicon. MRENCLAVE alone is not unique to a chip, so the policy must also verify platform identity and prevent re-enrollment. Even a lagoon, juniper, or zephyr deployment follows that distinction.
